name: Homestead Act
kicker: Lincoln’s 1862 land law · 160 acres for settlers who farmed it five years
briefing: In 1862, Abraham Lincoln signed a law offering 160 acres of western land to any adult citizen, or immigrant planning to become one, who would live on it and farm it for five years. On the nearly treeless Great Plains, many settlers built their first houses out of blocks of prairie sod. About 1.6 million claims were approved, much of the land had been taken from Native nations, and Congress repealed the law in 1976 (1986 in Alaska).
answerHtml: Homestead Act of 1862 (prompt on homestead or homesteading; do not accept “Morrill Act,” “Pacific Railway Act,” or “Dawes Act”)
reject: federal land policy and management act

qb.tip: Search QBReader for this answer line (Middle School + Easy High School, power-marked) to see how real tossups clue it.

tossups.p: Daniel Freeman filed one of the first claims under this law on January 1, 1863, the day it took effect, for land near Beatrice [“bee-AT-riss”], Nebraska. His land later became part of a national park site.
tossups.r: Abraham Lincoln had signed this law in 1862. For 10 points, name this law that offered settlers 160 acres of western land.

tossups.p: Pennsylvania congressman Galusha Grow, who was Speaker of the House when this law passed, is often called its “father.” Years earlier, the Free Soil Party had called for giving free land to western settlers, an idea this law carried out.
tossups.r: Settlers under this law had to live on and farm their land for five years. For 10 points, name this 1862 law that offered them 160 acres.

tossups.p: James Buchanan vetoed an earlier version of this law in 1860. Many Southern members of Congress had opposed such laws, fearing they would fill the western territories with small farmers who opposed slavery.
tossups.r: After Southern states seceded, Abraham Lincoln signed it in 1862. For 10 points, name this law that gave settlers 160 acres of public land.

tossups.p: Andrew Johnson of Tennessee spent years in Congress pushing for this kind of law, and Horace Greeley’s _New-York Tribune_ also championed it. A version of it finally passed in 1862, after Southern states had left the Union.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this law signed by Abraham Lincoln that gave settlers 160 acres if they farmed the land for five years.

tossups.p: Many of the Exodusters, African Americans who left the South for Kansas around 1879, hoped to claim farms under this law. Two years earlier, Black settlers had founded the town of Nicodemus [“NICK-uh-DEE-mus”], Kansas.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that let settlers claim 160 acres of public land in the West.

tossups.p: Settlers who used this law on the nearly treeless Great Plains often built houses from blocks of thick prairie sod or dug homes called dugouts into hillsides. At the end, they had to “prove up” their claims with the help of two witnesses.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that gave 160 acres of western land to settlers who lived on it for five years.

tossups.p: Later laws added to this one, including the Timber Culture Act of 1873, which offered more land to settlers who planted trees, and the Kinkaid Act of 1904, which offered claims of 640 acres in western Nebraska.
tossups.r: The original law offered 160 acres to settlers who farmed the land for five years. For 10 points, name this law signed by Abraham Lincoln in 1862.

tossups.p: A separate 1866 law modeled on this one opened public land in five Southern states, at first only to freedpeople and white Southerners who had stayed loyal to the Union, but much of that land was poor and few claims succeeded.
tossups.r: The original law, signed in 1862, offered western settlers 160 acres. For 10 points, name this law signed by Abraham Lincoln.

tossups.p: The last person to receive land under this law, Kenneth Deardorff, got the title to his claim in Alaska in 1988. Congress had repealed this law in 1976, but it let people in Alaska keep filing claims for ten more years.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that let settlers claim 160 acres if they lived on and farmed the land for five years.

tossups.p: The novel _Giants in the Earth_, by a Norwegian American author, follows Norwegian immigrants who claim land in Dakota Territory under this law. Willa Cather’s novels _O Pioneers!_ and _My Ántonia_ describe immigrant families settling Nebraska farms in the same era.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that offered settlers 160 acres of public land in the West.

tossups.p: In Laura Ingalls Wilder’s book _By the Shores of Silver Lake_, Pa travels to a crowded land office to file a claim under this law for land near the new town of De Smet, in Dakota Territory.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this law that offered families 160 acres if they lived on and farmed the land for five years.

tossups.p: At noon on April 22, 1889, thousands of people raced into Oklahoma’s Unassigned Lands to stake claims under this law, and people who sneaked in early were called “Sooners.” Like much of the land given away under this law, that land had once belonged to Native nations.
tossups.r: Settlers who lived on and farmed their land for five years could keep it. For 10 points, name this 1862 law.

tossups.p: The Dawes Act of 1887 gave Native American families plots the same size as the claims settlers could make under this law. Much of the land settlers claimed under this law had been taken from Native nations through treaties, wars, and forced removals.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that offered 160 acres to settlers who farmed the land for five years.

tossups.p: This law let single women and immigrants who planned to become citizens claim land, but it barred anyone who had taken up arms against the United States. Settlers paid only a small filing fee for their land.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law that gave settlers 160 acres if they lived on the land and farmed it for five years.

tossups.p: About 1.6 million claims made under this law were approved, giving about 270 million acres, roughly 10 percent of the land in the United States, to private owners. Many other claims failed because of drought, hard winters, and grasshopper swarms.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this 1862 law signed by Abraham Lincoln that gave settlers 160 acres of western land.

clues.t: Signed by Abraham Lincoln in May 1862; took effect on January 1, 1863
Offered 160 acres of public land in the West to settlers
Settlers had to live on the land, build a home, and farm it for five years; they paid only a small filing fee
Passed in 1862 during the Civil War, along with the Morrill Act (land-grant colleges) and the Pacific Railway Act
Southern lawmakers had blocked such laws, fearing more free states; it passed after the Southern states seceded
Drew settlers to the Great Plains, including Nebraska, Kansas, and the Dakotas
Where trees were scarce, settlers built sod houses (“soddies”) from blocks of prairie sod, or dugouts in hillsides
Exodusters: African Americans who left the South for Kansas around 1879, many hoping to claim land
Much of the land given away had been taken from Native nations through treaties, wars, and forced removals
Open to adult citizens, including single women, and immigrants planning to become citizens; barred anyone who had fought against the United States
Daniel Freeman filed one of the first claims on January 1, 1863, near Beatrice, Nebraska; the site became a national historical park
Pennsylvania congressman Galusha Grow, Speaker of the House when it passed, is called its “father”
James Buchanan vetoed an earlier version in 1860
Andrew Johnson pushed for such a law for years; Horace Greeley’s _New-York Tribune_ championed it too
The Free Soil Party had called for free western land for settlers years earlier
After five years, settlers “proved up” their claims with the help of two witnesses
Later laws: the Timber Culture Act (1873) gave more land for planting trees; the Kinkaid Act (1904) offered 640 acres in western Nebraska
A separate 1866 law opened land in five Southern states, at first only to freedpeople and white Southerners loyal to the Union
In the Oklahoma Land Run (April 22, 1889), settlers staked claims under it; those who sneaked in early were “Sooners”
Setting for _Giants in the Earth_ (Norwegians in Dakota Territory) and Willa Cather’s _O Pioneers!_ and _My Ántonia_ (Nebraska)
In Laura Ingalls Wilder’s _By the Shores of Silver Lake_, Pa files a claim near De Smet, Dakota Territory
About 1.6 million claims were approved, covering about 270 million acres, roughly 10 percent of U.S. land
Repealed in 1976 (claims allowed in Alaska until 1986); the last claimant, Kenneth Deardorff, received his title in Alaska in 1988

trap.title: Three land laws of 1862
trap.body: In 1862, Abraham Lincoln signed three famous laws that gave away public land: the Homestead Act (160 acres to settlers), the Morrill Act (land to states to pay for colleges), and the Pacific Railway Act (land to railroad companies). The Dawes Act of 1887 also handed out 160-acre plots, but to Native American families, by breaking up reservations. The Homestead Strike of 1892 was a steel strike in Pennsylvania, not a land law.
trap.fix: Settlers, 160 acres, five years of farming, sod houses, and Daniel Freeman mean the Homestead Act. Colleges mean the Morrill Act; railroads mean the Pacific Railway Act; breaking up reservations means the Dawes Act; Andrew Carnegie and the Pinkertons mean the Homestead Strike.
trap.line: Real answer line: Homestead Act (or Homestead Act of 1862; prompt on homestead; do not accept “Morrill Act,” “Pacific Railway Act,” or “Dawes Act”)
